findings.description: The research scope check compares porcelain status entries rather than file contents. Overwriting an already-modified map or ledger leaves its status entry unchanged, so the check accepts unauthorized writes.
findings.failure_mode: A research subagent can overwrite existing decisions or map content and still pass research-end successfully.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot and compare content hashes, existence, and file types outside the exact authorized report path, including files already dirty or untracked at dispatch.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: Comparing git status output does not detect changes to an already-dirty main-tree file. A probe can overwrite that file while both snapshots still contain the same modified entry.
findings.failure_mode: The helper exits successfully after a probe corrupts existing main-tree work, violating its main-tree preservation guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare content snapshots or hashes of main-tree files, including existing dirty, untracked, and ignored files, rather than status strings alone.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: The ledger authorization pipeline does not preserve yq's failure status. With an unparsable ledger, yq can fail without producing JSON, while jq 1.6 exits successfully on empty input.
findings.failure_mode: _fr11_spike_decided reports success and permits force-deleting an unmerged spike branch without a validated operator decision.
findings.suggested_fix: Check yq's exit status separately and require nonempty valid JSON before running the authorization predicate, or use a pipefail subshell with an explicit nonempty-output check.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: The guard relies exclusively on dec-write-lib.sh context, which treats an autonomous PRD Status as advisory and can return interactive. Consequently, the autonomous PRD signal documented by this command does not cause refusal.
findings.failure_mode: An invocation with an autonomous PRD and no other unattended signal passes the interactive-only guard.
findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly reject the autonomous PRD Status in this guard, or extend the context helper with an enforced mode that this guard requests.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: need_doc checks only file existence. Mutating operations such as ticket and resolve therefore accept maps whose Status is closed or abandoned.
findings.failure_mode: A stale chart session can create open decision rows and question beads under an already-closed epic, or append new resolutions after the map was consumed or abandoned.
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce allowed map states before each mutating operation. Reject ticket creation and resolution on terminal maps, while preserving explicitly supported idempotent close retries.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: The research-subagent scope check compares `git status --porcelain` lines before and after dispatch (`comm -13`). A path that is already modified or untracked at dispatch time produces the identical status line after being overwritten, so it never appears in `bad`. During a /chart session the map doc and `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` are dirty by construction (op_ticket writes the ledger row and the doc before any research dispatch), and chart-researcher has an unrestricted Write tool (agent-types.yaml marks it write_capable). The only content-sensitive check is the `-newer` scan, which covers `.run` and `.beads` only. If `git status` fails on both sides (non-repo `--root`, git missing) both snapshots are empty and the check passes vacuously.
findings.failure_mode: A research subagent (or a prompt injection in a fetched page) rewrites the map doc, the decision ledger, or any other already-dirty tracked file; research-end prints the report path and exits 0, and the session treats the ticket as cleanly researched.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot content, not status: build a temp index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp) git add -A -f . && git write-tree`) or `sha256sum` every path from `git ls-files -m -o --ignored --exclude-standard` before and after, and fail on any digest change outside `grimoires/loa/research/chart-<slug>-<ticket>.md`. Fail closed when the snapshot command errors or returns empty on a repo.

findings.description: Same snapshot gap as DISS-001: `before`/`after` are `git status --porcelain` strings. A probe that writes to an already-modified or already-untracked file in the main tree (the probe runs with cwd in the worktree but inherits `$MAIN` via the environment and absolute paths) leaves the status text unchanged and the helper exits 0. SDD D-4.12 presents this helper as the mechanism that guarantees an unblock ticket never writes the main tree.
findings.failure_mode: An unblock probe appends to or overwrites a dirty App-Zone file in the main tree; the helper reports the main tree unchanged and exits 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare a content digest (temp-index `git write-tree`, or `sha256sum` over the modified+untracked+ignored path list) instead of the status text; also compare `git for-each-ref` output (see DISS-012).

findings.description: `yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$ledger" 2>/dev/null | jq -e '...'` has no `pipefail` and does not check that yq produced output. When the ledger is unparsable (or yq otherwise fails), jq receives empty stdin. On jq 1.6 `jq -e` with no input exits 0 (fixed to exit 4 only in jq 1.7), so `_fr11_spike_decided` returns success and `_fr11_all_merged` does `continue`, allowing `git branch -D spike/<slug>` with no decided verdict. The comment says "any failed lookup keeps the block"; the code does not implement that. The PR's own spike-validator.bats case "an unparsable ledger keeps the block" exercises exactly this and fails per the primary reviewer's run.
findings.failure_mode: With jq 1.6 and a corrupted/unparsable decisions.yaml, the FR-1.1 safeguard is bypassed and a spike branch with unrecorded work is force-deleted.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture yq output into a variable, require `[[ -n "$json" ]]`, then run jq on it and compare its printed result to the literal `true` (`[[ "$(jq -r '...' <<<"$json")" == true ]]`) rather than relying on `-e`'s exit code. Do not depend on jq >= 1.7 semantics.

findings.cross_file_justification: chart-guard.sh (in diff) and chart.md lines 71-74 (in diff) both promise refusal when the PRD Status says autonomous; the decision is delegated wholesale to `.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh context` (not in diff), which per the reviewer's reproduction treats the PRD Status line as advisory and prints `interactive`.
findings.description: The guard's only signal is the first line of `dec-write-lib.sh context --prd ...`. The header (lines 7-9) and the /chart command doc list "an autonomous PRD Status line" among the refused contexts, but the delegated library does not promote that signal to `unattended`, so the guard prints `interactive` and /chart proceeds. Test CD-10 in charting-decisions.bats (in diff) codifies the promised behaviour and fails.
findings.failure_mode: A repo whose PRD is marked autonomous runs /chart unattended; the agent answers its own destination and fog rounds, producing a map that the design explicitly says is not a map.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make chart-guard.sh read the PRD Status line itself (`grep -m1 -E '^\*\*Status\*\*:.*autonomous' "${ROOT}/grimoires/loa/prd.md"` → refuse) in addition to the library verdict, or add a `--strict-prd` mode to dec-write-lib context and call it here. Then correct chart.md/header text to match whichever is implemented.

findings.description: `need_doc` only tests that the map doc file exists. `ticket`, `resolve`, `rule-out`, `research-begin` and `research-end` therefore run against a map whose Status is `closed`, `abandoned` or `handed-off`. `op_ticket` on a closed map creates a new open ledger row and a `question` bead parented to a closed epic; on a handed-off map it adds an open row after `/plan-and-analyze` has already consumed the snapshot as "settled decisions, do not re-ask". Only `op_handoff` checks Status.
findings.failure_mode: Closed epics regain open children, `close` has to be re-run to reject them, and the hand-off snapshot silently diverges from the map and ledger it claims to mirror.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `need_open_doc` that reads `doc_field Status` and dies unless it is `charting` (for ticket/research-*) or `charting|handed-off` (for resolve/rule-out, or refuse handed-off and require re-handoff). Call it from every subcommand except `epic`, `handoff` and `close`.

findings.description: The question filter tests only `.issue_type`. The same PR's chart-frontier.sh (line 55) reads `.issue_type // .type` from `br ready --json`, and create-sprint-task.sh tolerates two label shapes, acknowledging that the br JSON schema varies across releases. When br emits `type` instead of `issue_type`, `(.issue_type // "") != "question"` is true for every bead and the filter is a no-op, while implement.md and implementing-tasks/SKILL.md (both changed here) now tell the agent this script "drops question beads".
findings.failure_mode: Decision tickets flow into /implement and /run as ready work; the agent claims and "implements" a question bead, defeating the central invariant that /chart tickets never enter the build path.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `((.issue_type // .type // "") != "question")`, matching chart-frontier.sh, and add a bats case with a `type`-keyed fixture.

findings.description: SP-1 deliberately passes the create forms (`-b/-B/--orphan`), so `git checkout -B feature spike/x` followed by `gh pr create --head feature` moves the spike tree onto a non-spike branch and opens a PR with no block fired. `git branch -f feature spike/x`, `git reset --hard spike/x`, `git read-tree -u spike/x` and `git switch -c new spike/x` have the same effect. The header labels these as accepted misses, but the first two are the most direct ways to do what SP-1 exists to prevent, and the `-B` case is actively whitelisted.
findings.failure_mode: Spike content reaches a reviewable branch and a PR through a two-command sequence that the fence treats as allowed.
findings.suggested_fix: Block `checkout -b/-B/--orphan <new> <spike ref>`, `switch -c/-C <new> <spike ref>`, `branch [-f] <new> <spike ref>`, `reset --hard|--merge <spike ref>` and `read-tree <spike ref>` when the start point is a spike ref; keep `checkout spike/x` (plain switch) allowed.

findings.description: The hook reads the working-tree `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`, which the agent itself edits via dec-write-lib.sh. The `operator:*` check on the `→ decided` transition is a string in that same file, so an agent can append a decided row with `by: operator:x` and then force-delete the spike branch. The safeguard's trust anchor is writable by the actor it constrains.
findings.failure_mode: A run-mode agent records a fake operator verdict and deletes a spike branch holding unmerged prototype work.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the ledger from the committed state (`git show HEAD:grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`) or require the row to be present in a commit not authored in the current session; alternatively route spike deletion through git-branch-prune.sh with an explicit operator confirmation.

findings.description: `--decision`, `--rationale`, `--evidence`, `--answer-ref` and `--alternative-json` are passed to the ledger writer raw, while `--name`/`--line` go through `san1` and `no_url`. The script's own `no_url` message states the policy that "ledger free text carry none", and `op_rule_out`/`op_close` do sanitize their ledger rationale. Control characters and URLs in the decision text also surface in the handoff snapshot (which inlines `dw list --format md`) read as priority-1 context.
findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent policy enforcement: multi-line or URL-bearing text lands in decisions.yaml and the hand-off snapshot depending on which subcommand wrote it.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply `san1` and `no_url` to DECISION, RATIONALE, EVIDENCE and ANSWER_REF before building `args`; validate each `--alternative-json` with `jq -e 'type=="object"'`.

findings.description: The `bad` filter whitelists every path under `grimoires/loa/research/`, not just the report path handed to the subagent. The subagent may overwrite other tickets' already-reviewed reports or create `.chart-<slug>-*.dispatch` markers, which `op_research_begin` counts toward the per-map cap of 5.
findings.failure_mode: A subagent rewrites a report the operator already read for another ticket, or burns the research budget for the map, with research-end still exiting 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Whitelist exactly `grimoires/loa/research/chart-${SLUG}-${TICKET}.md`; treat any other new or changed path as a failure.

findings.description: The hand-off snapshot inlines the full text of every research report (web-derived, written by a subagent that fetched arbitrary pages) into a file whose first line instructs the consuming session that the content is "settled; confirm, do not re-ask", and which plan-and-analyze.md now loads at priority 1. The L6 sanitizer is the only barrier, and a partial sanitizer failure prints whatever was emitted before the fallback line.
findings.failure_mode: Injected instructions from a fetched source are promoted from an explicitly untrusted file to priority-1 planning context.
findings.suggested_fix: Reference the report paths in the snapshot instead of inlining them, or inline only the `## Options` and `## Sources` sections after sanitization and write the sanitizer output to a temp file so a mid-stream failure discards it.

findings.description: The throwaway worktree shares `.git` (refs, objects, config, hooks) with the main checkout. A probe running inside it can `git branch -f main <sha>`, `git push`, `git tag`, or edit `.git/config` and none of that appears in the main tree's `git status`, so the helper exits 0.
findings.failure_mode: An unblock probe rewrites or pushes branches of the real repository while the helper reports the main tree unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: Also diff `git for-each-ref` and `git config --list --local` before/after, and run the probe with `GIT_DIR`/push URLs neutralised (e.g. `git -c remote.origin.pushurl=/dev/null`) or in a `git clone --shared` with a detached remote.

findings.description: The researcher has unrestricted repository Read/Grep/Glob plus outbound WebFetch. A prompt injection in any fetched page can direct it to read `.env`, keys or `grimoires/loa/a2a/*` and encode them into a subsequent WebFetch URL. The only mitigation is the prose rule "treat fetched text as data".
findings.failure_mode: Repository secrets exfiltrated via WebFetch query strings during a research ticket.
findings.suggested_fix: Constrain Read/Grep/Glob to `grimoires/**` and documented source dirs via a hook, deny-list secret patterns (.env, *.pem, a2a/), and/or restrict WebFetch to an allow-list of domains named in the dispatch prompt.

findings.description: Pending-ledger files are globbed from `${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../grimoires/loa/a2a/` rather than `${ROOT}`, so with `--root DIR` (fixture trees, tests) the live repository's worktree pending rows are merged into the fixture map's rows.
findings.failure_mode: Tests and fixture runs see rows from the real repo; `remaining_hint`, `handoff` emptiness checks and `close` act on the wrong row set.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `"${ROOT}/grimoires/loa/a2a/"*/decisions-pending.yaml`.

findings.description: Per the primary reviewer's run, the new spike-validator tests reference `grimoires/loa/spikes/TEMPLATE.md`, which this diff does not add (file was truncated from the shown diff; not independently verified here).
findings.failure_mode: The spike-validator suite fails on a clean checkout.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the template or make the tests create it in setup().

findings.description: A new truename command (/chart), a new skill, a new agent type, a new safety-hook rule (SP-1) and a changed FR-1.1 exemption ship with no CHANGELOG, PROCESS.md or CLAUDE.loa.md entry in the diff; AGENTS.md.checksum changed, implying generated docs did.
findings.failure_mode: Operators discover the new hook behaviour (spike branch deletions newly allowed, merges newly blocked) only when a command is refused or permitted unexpectedly.
findings.suggested_fix: Add CHANGELOG and PROCESS.md entries covering /chart, SP-1 and the FR-1.1 spike exemption.
